cases.reason: The reader saw that 2002 CONTROL 'differs only in ... OCCURS subjects' and dismissed it. That difference matters here. 2023 CONTROL SR3 forbids a control subject to any OCCURS clause. 2002 CONTROL has no such rule (SR3 says only 'may be qualified'; SR5 bars only a subordinate variable-occurrence entry), and in 2002 a data-name operand includes subscription if needed (5.1.3; 2014 E.2 item 25). So CONTROL IS T-C(1) is a one-operand 2002 CONTROL clause, and SR11 permits the CF operand to be omitted under it. That is a 2002 case the 2023 row cannot reach. Probe ctl_sub1.cob is refused at --std 2002 with COBOL1699, which cites 2023 SR3. This is the same family as the p-01/p-09 RECORD KEY overturns.

This has the same cause as SR11. 'Each control data item' in 2002 includes subscripted controls such as CONTROLS ARE T-C(1) T-C(2), which are legal because 2002 has no OCCURS ban (5.1.3; 2014 E.2 item 25; 2023 CONTROL SR3 is new). SR14 then permits one CF FOR T-C(1) and one CF FOR T-C(2), and forbids two CF FOR T-C(1). At --std 2002, ctl_sub2 is refused with COBOL1699 and also with COBOL2749 'second CONTROL FOOTING for control T-C', which treats two distinct control data items as one. ctl_sub3 is refused, which is right in outcome. One weakness: 2002 CONTROL SR6 ('data-name-1 shall be unique') is ambiguous for T-C(1) T-C(2), but CONTROLS ARE T-C(1) X with one CF FOR T-C(1) still lies in this rule's 2002 scope.
